title: Semiparametric Efficiency Bound for Staggered Triple Differences with Covariates

proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted to prove that the covariate-varying aggregate loading b-star applied to the OVS score vector is itself the published-class canonical gradient. Tangent exhaustion instead exposed additional period-specific normal directions: the sound finite-support result projects a reference score onto the complete OVS normal space, while b-star remains only aggregate-family optimal. The repaired note retains pointwise finite-support attainment and gap inference, but the promised kernel, continuous-covariate extension, rank-changing inference, and package implementation remain unresolved.
tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, this note proves the full-data/observed-law image for arbitrary covariate support.  At fixed finite-support covariate laws it exhausts the observed tangent normal generated by every period-admissible clean cohort and derives the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) remains only the optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family and is canonical exactly when its published-normal equation holds.  A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and a finite-support moment map gives pointwise Wald inference for comparator efficiency gaps away from equality and rank changes.  In the corrected bounded binary witness, the best joint constant loading loses exactly \(3/512\) and the published componentwise OVS loading loses \(15/512\), both relative to the published bound.
gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and Remark 4.6) establish identification, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and constant componentwise GMM optimality but leave semiparametric efficiency in overidentified DDD models open. The closest staggered-DiD efficiency result proves observational equivalence before projecting, and the closest DDD influence-function result is just identified.
fill: The paper first constructs every target, residual, covariance, rank, and spectrum from observed-law primitives, then proves full-data extendability and exact tangent exhaustion. It next derives the fixed-rank canonical gradient and bound, selects the unknown rank by foldwise thresholding, proves covariance and loading rates in discrete and Hölder-series regimes, constructs an attaining cross-fitted estimator, and gives globally defined comparator loadings with an observable equality diagnostic. The efficiency-gap functional has an explicit pathwise derivative, Moore--Penrose KKT contribution, projected-score sieve implementation, and pointwise Wald limit away from equality.
